prompt:
A miniature painting from a Gothic illuminated manuscript, a Book of Hours made around 1400, used as the background of a 2D narrative game.

Technique: opaque egg tempera and gouache on parchment, applied in flat, even areas of pure mineral colour: deep lapis-lazuli ultramarine, vermilion, rose pink, malachite and verdigris green, yellow ochre, lead white and soft blue-greys. Every shape is outlined with a fine, even dark-brown pen line. Modelling only with a few flat darker strokes and fine parallel white highlight lines on folds and edges, as in manuscript painting; no cast shadows, no soft gradients, no atmospheric haze, no light effects, no glow.

Space and drawing: flat medieval space without true perspective. The ground plane tilts steeply upward as if seen from high above, so the sea rises like a wall behind the quay. Buildings are small, simplified doll's-house blocks shown from two sides at once in naive perspective, smaller than they would really be. The sea is a flat surface of deep blue-green covered with neat, repeating rows of small curled white wavelets, like a decorative pattern. The rocky headland is built of stylized stepped rock ledges with flat tops and vertical faces, pale grey-violet and ochre, with a few tufts of grass. The boats are simple wooden hulls with one mast each, drawn in side view.

Sky: instead of a natural sky, the upper part of the picture is a flat burnished gold-leaf ground: a smooth, bright yellow-gold area with a fine tooled diaper pattern of small punched stars and dots (the first stars are these punched gold stars). Between the gold ground and the horizon lies a band of stylized ultramarine clouds with scalloped edges, and directly above the horizon a narrow, flat vermilion-orange band for the dusk.

Effects: the lighthouse lamp is only a small flat gold-and-vermilion flame in its lantern room, without any beam, rays or halo; no smoke from the chimney; no birds in the sky (these are animated separately).

Composition (percentages of the image size): the horizon lies at about 40 % of the image height; the gold ground fills the image above about 22 % of the height. The cottage stands on the left, from the left edge to about 20 % of the width. The headland with the lighthouse fills the right side from about 70 % of the width; the lighthouse stands at about 82 % of the width. The quay is a tilted paved band across the whole width from about 72 % of the image height to the bottom edge; the middle of the quay from 22 % to 50 % of the width is completely empty, because a large figure will stand there. The jetty and the two boats lie on the water between about 45 % and 68 % of the width. The lantern post stands at the back edge of the quay at about 60 % of the width; the barrels, the crates and the coil of rope stand at the right end of the quay, from about 75 % to 97 % of the width. The picture runs edge to edge: no border, no frame, no margin and no parchment around it (the game adds its own page, frame and lettering).

Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a modern fantasy illustration, not a children's book, not an oil painting with realistic light: a flat, decorative, precisely painted Gothic manuscript miniature with clear outlines and gleaming gold.

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

It raises the paw on the right side of the picture beside its head in the speaking gesture of medieval painting: the forearm upright, the palm turned outwards to the viewer, the index finger and the middle finger extended upwards, the other fingers folded. The raised forearm and paw stand free against the background, clearly separated from the head and the cap by a gap. The shirt sleeve of the raised arm is rolled up and ends in a thick cuff at the elbow; the forearm comes out of this cuff. The other arm holds the parcel against the body.
